# Questions and their numbers

Generated by `scripts/reported/emit_reported_values.py` from the question
list (`src/continuum_swr_replay/reported/questions.py`) and the summaries
(`paper/reported/<summary>.json`); do not edit by hand. Cite a value in
`paper/main.tex` by its macro. A value marked *pending* may not be quoted
as a finding. A summary file is named for what it holds; a question's part
is where the paper reports it. *Builder function* names the function in
`src/continuum_swr_replay/reported/<summary>.py`, or in a module of the
package `reported/<summary>/`, that names and describes a value. The
statistic is computed by the `analysis/` function it calls, or copied from
an input file; the builder itself only counts the size of an input. The
last section lists, for each builder function, the `analysis/` functions
it calls.

## Part 2: the events are real

### 2c.3. Do an event's spikes favor its decoded location over the animal's position (against matched windows and on held-out tetrodes), and do held-out spikes favor a decoder that may be non-local outside SWRs over one that is non-local only in SWRs or never?

Status: computed. Figures: 2, 2j, S2c, S2d, S2e. Values: 506.

*Note:* Two lines of evidence. The spike evidence: the matched-window, likelihood-advantage and held-out tetrode values (the held-out tetrode score of Figure 2's supplement, panel S2c, is the *_heldout_gain_*, *_heldout_spiking_gain_* and *_heldout_control_gain_* values; panel S2d, shared content, is the *_shared_content_* values: the held-out agreement per spike of the events by the spread of the other tetrodes' estimate, in bins fixed in advance). The decoder comparison: the restriction_* values compare the local-only, SWR-only and full decoders by held-out predictive score, over immobile time (restriction_immobile_* and restriction_outside_swr_*; Figure 2j draws each decoder's gain over the local-only decoder and the full minus the SWR-only decoder over all immobile time and outside SWRs; Figure 2's supplement draws that gain outside SWRs away from the SWRs (S2e); its shares in the events detected from the held-out decode and outside them and the gain at well-sampled places are for the text) and over the events detected from the held-out decode (restriction_heldout_*) or the canonical events (restriction_canonical_non_swr_* and restriction_canonical_swr_*); the *_found_again and *_with_canonical values say how those two sets of events agree. The held-out test split by SWR (the values whose keys start heldout_swr_ or heldout_non_swr_) was made by the tracked scripts/event_evidence/split_state_evidence_by_swr.py at commit e78273b5 (the run's provenance file, read 2026-11-11); the retired claims table called these values pending.

| `\EventsRestrictionOutsideSwrFullMinusSwrShareInHeldoutNonSwrEvents` | 93 % |  | one-step-ahead (filter) predictive log score of each 2 ms bin's spikes, with each of five folds of whole trials (balanced by destination well; a trial's run to a well with its whole stay there, when longer than 30 s, is cut into pieces of at most 30 s that can fall in different folds) scored under a decoder whose place-field encodings were fit on the decode's training bins (outside every SWR and artifact) of the other folds, more than 1 s from the fold, and whose state transitions and initial conditions were fit by EM with the fold's bins missing; the gain is the score under the full decoder (every state at every bin) minus under the SWR-only decoder (only the non-local states in SWR bins, only the local states elsewhere). Per epoch, the gain summed over the events detected from the held-out decode with no SWR (their immobile bins outside SWRs (outside every SWR of the source, where SWR detection was observed) inside a well visit; an event that runs past the final poke-out adds its bins before it only), divided by the gain summed over every one of the epoch's immobile bins outside SWRs (outside every SWR of the source, where SWR detection was observed) inside a well visit (no value when that sum is not positive). Both are signed sums, so a share can be above 1 or below 0 and the two shares need not add to 1. ### 2d.9. How do per-event spike count, MUA z-score and active tetrodes compare across non-SWR events, SWR events and matched immobile non-event windows?

Status: computed. Figures: 2, 2h. Values: 33.

*Note:* Was question 2c.2: events are detected from spiking, so more spikes than a quiet window is not evidence of spatial content.

- Processed-Data/event_participation (scripts/event_evidence/measure_event_participation.py)
- Processed-Data/event_spike_evidence/*/event_spike_evidence_metrics.parquet (every event, no cap), each scored event matched to the event table by epoch and start, with each epoch's well visits
